title: Multimodal Burst Sculpting and Kernel Compatibility Playbook
author: Priya Nandakumar
body:
Purpose

This playbook documents an operational and profiling approach for handling short, high-concurrency multimodal bursts (text + embeddings + image preprocessing calls) while minimizing SLO violations and quantization/kernel compatibility regressions. It synthesizes: runtime admission-probing patterns, sculpting heuristics, a kernel compatibility checklist, profiling recipes, an e2e microbenchmark procedure, and an emergency rollback checklist.

Scope

- Audience: serving-runtime engineers, oncall, benchmarking team, release engineers.
- When to use: recurring tail spikes, sudden customer traffic bursts, onboarding new kernel variants, mixed-modes workload rollouts.
- Not covered: long-running batch offline training jobs or non-inference control-plane operations.

Background and motivation

We observe two recurring failure modes during multimodal bursts:
1) Admission storms that saturate kernel slots and trigger tail latency cascades.
2) New kernel variants (quantized or optimized tensor cores) that change memory patterns and produce silent fidelity regressions under burst conditions.

This playbook gives precise steps to identify which of the two is dominant and safe mitigations to restore SLOs while preserving throughput and unit cost.

Key SLOs and operational thresholds

- Short-request SLO (p95): 120 ms for <128 token text generations (hosted tier).
- Long-request SLO (p95): 1.2 s for sequences up to 2048 tokens.
- Embedding request SLO (p95): 60 ms.
- Kernel admission queue length: critical at > 200 pending kernel ops per GPU (investigate), emergency at > 400 (start mitigation).
- GPU kernel timeout failure rate: target < 0.01% 5m rolling.

Definitions

- Sculpting: active admission shaping that reduces concurrency or steers requests to compatible model variants during a burst.
- Admission probe: lightweight synthetic call that tests a kernel-path’s tail behavior without consuming full token budgets.
- Compatibility score: heuristic (0–100) combining memory pressure, float-precision support, and KV cache layout alignment.

Operational overview

1) Detection
- Alert triggers: sustained p95 breach for short-request SLO for 2 consecutive minutes OR kernel queue length above critical threshold.
- Dashboards: Burst Signatures dashboard (team: runtime-observability) shows per-model sequence-length histogram, per-GPU queue depth, kernel latency CDF, and KV cache hit ratio.

2) Triage (fast path)
- Step 1: Confirm burst shape. Oncall runs the lightweight probe (see CLI below) against affected model ID.
  - CLI: curl -s -X POST https://runtime-diagnostic.internal/api/v1/diagnose
    -d '{"model":"<model-id>","probe_type":"admission","seq_len":16,"modes":["text"]}'
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $DIAG_TOKEN"
- Step 2: Inspect kernel-level telemetry: top kernels by p99 latency, GPU mem utilization, and preemption events (from /metrics/kernel_events).
- Step 3: If kernel p99 spikes with normal request arrival, classify as admission saturation. If kernel p95 stable but per-request latency increases along with memory-related OOMs or soft-evictions, classify as kernel-compat/fidelity issue.

3) Immediate mitigations
- Admission saturation mitigation (fast):
  a) Ramp per-tenant concurrency limit down by 50% using the admission controller API: POST /runtime/admission/patch {"tenant":"<tenant-id>","max_concurrency":<value>}
  b) Enable short-path fallback: route requests with seq_len<=32 to low-latency variant (if model pinned variants exist).
  c) Turn on prefix-kv-cache bypass for bursty tenants to reduce KV cache pressure (command in runbook section).
- Kernel compatibility mitigation (fast):
  a) Disable the kernel variant tagged as experimental on affected pool: PATCH /runtime/kernels/<kernel-id>/state {"enabled":false}
  b) Switch to software-safeguarded kernel: set kernel_hint=legacy_safety on pool config.
  c) If memory ephemerality is suspected, reduce per-request beam/num_returned to shrink working set.

4) Recovery verification
- Run the admission probe and a short synthetic replay (10–20 requests across modes) to confirm p95 restored.
- Monitor rolling 10-minute window for regressions.

Profiling recipes (detailed)

A. Admission-probing recipe
1) Run the admission probe (as above) for the affected model across three modes: text-only (seq_len=16), text-long (seq_len=512), embeddings.
2) Capture the following traces: kernel selection path, scheduler decision, admission token. Annotate traces with request provenance tag: probe/admission/<run-id>.
3) Expected outputs: kernel queue depth waveform, preemption counts, per-kernel p50/p95/p99. Any kernel with p99 > 2x baseline flagged.

B. Memory-residency check (KV + activations)
1) For the offending node: run envoy/agent diagnostic endpoint to dump active KV footprint: GET /diagnostics/kv_footprint?node=<node-id>
2) Compare footprints across nodes to identify shard skew. If a node has >25% higher KV footprint than peers, mark for eviction and redistribute.

C. Kernel probe under synthetic microburst
1) Use the local microbench tool (examples below) to replay a 30s burst with configurable concurrency and inter-arrival jitter. Capture kernel traces and GPU metrics.
2) Run a grid of (concurrency: 2,8,32,128) x (seq_len: 16,128,512) and produce a CSV with p50/p95/p99 and memory high-water mark.

Example microbench (Python, simplified)
- python3 microbench/run_burst.py --model <model-id> --modes text,embed --concurrency 32 --seq-len 128 --duration 30 --output burst-run-<id>.csv

Kernel compatibility checklist (table)

| Kernel tag | Supported ops | Float precision | KV cache layout | Fallback severity |
|---|---:|---|---|---:|
| tensorcore-opt-v2 | fused-attn,matmul | fp16/amp | compact-interleaved | high |
| tc-legacy-safety | attn,matmul | fp32 only | legacy-offset | low |
| quant-int8-mode | matmul,quant-dequant | int8 | compact-interleaved | medium |
| hybrid-tc-async | attn,matmul,kv_prefetch | fp16/amp | split-shard | medium |

Interpretation notes:
- high fallback severity: disabling will likely increase token cost significantly or increase latency due to software fallback.
- Check the kernel runtime annotations for known issues (see related_pages).

Benchmarking and gating protocol for kernel rollouts

Before enabling a kernel variant across a pool, the rollout owner must execute the following in the staging footprint and record artifacts in the Benchmark Runbook:
1) Synthetic grid described in Profiling recipes, capturing p50/p95/p99, memory high-water marks, and preemption events.
2) Multitenant shadow run: replay 30-minute captured production trace with the kernel under test enabled on 10% of nodes. Measure SLO delta vs baseline.
3) Economic impact analysis: delta cost per token under realistic batching assumptions.
4) Compatibility matrix fill-out: confirm supported ops and kv cache alignment for all model families expected in the pool.

Rollout gates (must pass all)
- p95 regression < 2% relative to baseline for all seq_len bins.
- No new kernel-timeout errors in shadow run.
- Memory high-water mark < 90% of node RAM for 95% of runs.
- Quality regression tests: run canonical prompt set for the model family and ensure embedding cosine drift < 0.003 (or per-model guardrail).

Runbook snippets and commands

- Patch admission controller (safe):
  curl -X POST https://controlplane.internal/runtime/admission/patch
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $CP_TOKEN"
    -H "Content-Type: application/json"
    -d '{"selector":{"pool":"g4dn-multimodal"}, "patch":{"tenant_max_concurrency": 8}}'

- Disable kernel quickly (fast rollback):
  curl -X PATCH https://runtime.internal/kernels/tensorcore-opt-v2/state
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $OP_TOKEN"
    -H "Content-Type: application/json"
    -d '{"enabled": false, "reason":"auto-rollback:burst-induced-p99"}'

- Collect traces for a run id (example ktracer CLI):
  ktracer collect --run-id <run-id> --filters "model=<model-id>,tag=probe/admission" --out /tmp/traces.tgz

Escalation and ownership

- Primary owner: runtime-serving/team (oncall rotation). Contact: #runtime-oncall in Slack.
- Kernel rollout owner: release-kernel-team (owners list in kernel registry).
- If SLO remains violated after 20m of standard mitigations, escalate to SRE manager and Product (pages: /confluence/eng-sre/incident-review).

Post-incident tasks (postmortem checklist)

- Capture: traces, admission probe logs, microbench CSV, kernel registry state.
- Annotate: root-cause hypothesis: admission-saturation | kernel-compat | mem-skew | mixed.
- Action items: pinning changes, kernel-flag toggles, gating updates to rollout checklist.
- Run a targeted benchmark to validate fixes.

Artifacts and templates

- Microbench CSV template header: run_id,model_id,mode,concurrency,seq_len,p50_ms,p95_ms,p99_ms,mem_high_mark_mb,preemptions,kernel_id
- Postmortem template: incident-id,summary,timeline,root-cause,mitigations,actions,owners,due-dates

FAQ and troubleshooting tips

Q: Synthetic probes pass but production still sees p95 breach.
A: Check traffic shaping and tail correlation. Production may have correlated multimodal calls (image preprocessing + text gen) that the probe didn’t synthesize. Replay a live trace.

Q: Disabling kernel reduced throughput drastically.
A: Kernel had high fallback severity — use a gradual rollout policy and confirm a low-latency variant exists. Consider temporary additional capacity (spin-up dedicated burst nodes) while investigating.

Notes for future improvements

- Add an automated compatibility scoring service that computes compatibility score per model automatically and surfaces a per-pool warning when a kernel’s compatibility score drops under 70.
- Integrate microbench runs into CI as part of canary checks for kernel changes.

Appendix: useful internal endpoints and dashboards

- Burst Signatures dashboard: https://grafana.internal/d/burst-signatures
- Kernel events metrics: prometheus job name runtime-kernel-metrics
- Microbench tool repo: git@repo.internal:runtime/microbench.git
- Kernel registry: https://cargo.internal/kernels/registry
